parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the black-box C++ to Rust task, output layout, zero external crates, exact CLI parsing, bucket-count math, and byte-identical output requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated a workflow with a Spec phase of three scouts and later implement, verify, fix, and final agents; implementation ownership existed only after all scout results were awaited.
parallel.implementation: No implementation phase completed. The workflow remained in the spec/retry stage, so no Cargo project or test18.rs was delivered to the official artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow never assembled child findings into files, and artifact validation copied an empty directory after timeout.
parallel.verification: The workflow planned differential and build verifiers, but they were never reached; only exploratory child probes existed before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parallel run ended with returncode 143, empty final response, empty artifact file list, and 0 of 39 official tests passed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same CLI, numeric precision, stoi quirks, project layout, zero-dependency, and output formatting obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned investigation, implementation, build, verification, final artifact placement, and final explanation without delegating.
serial.implementation: It wrote Cargo.toml, test18.rs, and module files for hashing, growth, C++ compatibility, and hopscotch table behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It built both cargo and rustc outputs, left /output/test18 and the Cargo artifact tree, and the official artifact copy contained the expected files.
serial.verification: It ran cargo builds, unit tests, differential sweeps, malformed argument comparisons, random bounded fuzz, and final C++ versus Rust comparisons.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run noted the executable path caveat in final text, but the official artifact and evaluation passed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the same task requirements in the prompt and workflow context, including exact CLI, output bytes, zero crates, Cargo layout, black-box inference, and a compiled executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and documented the same requirements in its final summary after delivering files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was not the main difference; parallel failed to convert recognized requirements into a delivered implementation, while serial did.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into three spec scouts followed by implement, verifier, fixer, and final phases, but the implementer was scheduled only after all scout promises resolved.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained one continuous owner for probing, file creation, builds, tests, and final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel placed implementation behind an all-spec join; serial avoided that dependency and moved directly from discoveries into implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children detailed briefs and two scouts returned useful structured findings, but the stalled design retry received the same broad prompt without visible checkpoint inheritance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept findings in the same local context and used them directly while writing and validating the final files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost time across a retry boundary; serial did not have a transfer boundary where design work had to be restarted before implementation could proceed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did only exploratory probing and never produced the Cargo project or Rust source modules in the copied artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the complete project, including Cargo.toml, growth, hashing, C++ compatibility, hopscotch modules, and test18.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The official outcome diverged because serial delivered code while parallel timed out before implementation output existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Two scout results were recorded, but the design scout repeatedly stalled and no aggregate workflow result reached the parent before process kill.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; each local finding was consumed in the next implementation and verification actions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was blocked on a failed child retry chain; serial had no join boundary and reached final reporting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no final shared-state write collision, but it also had no integrated tree copied into the artifact directory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial populated the final shared output tree with source, executable, Cargo metadata, and build artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The shared-state issue was absence of integrated delivery in parallel, not conflicting writes; serial delivered a coherent artifact tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned differential and build verifiers after implementation, but the workflow never reached them and the official evaluator passed 0 of 39 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo build, cargo test, rustc, differential comparisons, bounded fuzz, and final C++/Rust comparisons, then passed 39 of 39 official tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had exploratory checks only and no final acceptance evidence; serial performed whole-deliverable checks before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2400 second budget, timed out with returncode 143, and closed with no final response or artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1922.659 seconds, had remaining budget, returned normally, and left a final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel retry chain exhausted closure time before delivery; serial completed under budget and submitted a passing artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The serial-only pass is explained by delivery, not by different task difficulty. Parallel understood much of the task and obtained useful scout findings, but its workflow kept implementation behind a blocking spec join. The hopscotch-design child was restarted without checkpointed progress and the workflow was killed before any implementation or final artifact was copied. Serial kept the same work in one trajectory, wrote the Rust project, built and tested it, and the official evaluator passed all 39 testcases.
parallel_contributors: Implementation was gated on all three spec scouts, and the hopscotch-design scout stalled and retried without a reusable checkpoint.
The workflow never reached its implement, verify, or final phases, so artifact validation copied an empty directory.
serial_contributors: The serial actor moved from probing into writing the Cargo project and Rust files within the same context.
The serial actor built with cargo and rustc, ran differential checks, and delivered the artifact tree before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No parallel coding defect is observable because parallel produced no final code; the material difference is that serial produced and verified code while parallel remained in orchestration.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned a later implementer; the problem was that the spec retry chain prevented reaching that owner.
No multiple component implementations existed to integrate because the implement phase never completed or returned code.
Final assembly was planned in the workflow after implementation; absence of deliverables followed from the blocked retry chain, not missing ownership.
The workflow script owned an end-to-end sequence from spec through final gate, but it stalled before later phases.
Implementation was blocked by a multi-scout spec join and retry, not by one mandatory serial preflight or oracle step.
The investigators overlapped, but the investigation phase did not complete and leave a shortened implementation window; it was trapped by an unchanged retry.
The indispensable path was not merely underallocated while auxiliaries ran; it was gated by a repeated uncheckpointed design retry.
The deadline was exhausted, but the specific causal boundary was the same child retry without checkpoint, not an independent broad fan-out episode.
The design prompt was broad, but the directly evidenced repeated failure was restarting it without checkpointed state; the scope issue is not retained separately.
The child briefs included the task source, black-box constraint, output layout, and edge-case obligations; the failure was retry state, not omitted known requirements.
No separately implemented components reached a point where absent file, API, or namespace contracts made them incompatible.
There is no evidence that a known finding was transferred and then omitted or truncated for a receiver; the stalled child never returned a usable handoff.
Large scout outputs existed, but no receiver failed to reduce an available bulky handoff before acting; implementation never started.
No actor consumed a superseded handoff and took an inconsistent next step; the workflow remained waiting on the spec join.
The available scout outputs contained corrections, but no incompatible returned contracts were jointly presented to an implementer and left unresolved.
The parent made no observable whole-task completion claim in the parallel run; final.txt is empty and the process timed out.

After the hopscotch-design scout stalled, retries received the same broad design prompt without visible checkpointed partial findings or a narrower next milestone, repeated investigation, and still failed before implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The repeated design retry consumed the remaining workflow window; implementation and verification never ran, and artifact validation copied no files.
candidates.near_match_reason: The run timed out, but the retained boundary is the retry lacking inherited checkpoint state rather than generic fan-out breadth or child count.

candidates.reason: The workflow and host timeout killed the run; there is no parent decision explicitly stopping a child before a needed finalized result.
No complete Rust candidate or mutually compatible component set existed for promotion; the implementation phase never ran.
No implementation change was merged after integrated verification; verification phases were not reached.
No delegated implementation completed or became retrievable, so there was no completed implementation result to join.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding because the workflow was still in Spec when it was killed.
The workflow did retry the stalled child; the harmful pattern is that those retries lacked checkpoint state, not that no retry or reassignment occurred at all.
The parent did not receive a complete aggregate workflow result; useful scout results remained below the unresolved workflow join rather than being visible and ignored by the parent.
The parent periodically inspected the journal and child progress; the defect was the unchanged retry gate, not waiting blindly without inspection.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation paths or files because implementation did not start.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source or configuration file.
There is no source file replacement or deletion event by another live owner in the parallel run.
No required executable, entry source, or submitted artifact was overwritten; no deliverable was produced.
The final artifact tree was empty rather than overwritten by cleanup, rebuild, or promotion.
Shared workspace write instability is not shown; the parallel children mainly performed read-only investigation and no shared implementation writes conflicted.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary artifact, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow restarted the same hopscotch-design investigation after stalls without passing a checkpoint, partial result, current workspace state, or narrower next milestone to the replacement. The retries repeated probing/design work, the parent kept waiting for the unresolved spec phase, and no implementation was delivered.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The repeated design retry consumed the remaining workflow window; implementation and verification never ran, and artifact validation copied no files.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Late Finalization were reviewed as near matches but not retained because they describe the same stalled-design retry chain or downstream terminal state.
